title: Tiered Residency Catalogue + Flexible Retention SLA Pilot for Enterprise Contracts
creator: Evelyn Tran
description: Run a pilot to offer a catalog of standardized data-residency tiers and configurable retention SLAs for enterprise contracts, paired with a pricing experiment that surfaces premium fees for stronger residency guarantees. Deliverables: (1) a public-facing residency catalogue with region/processing guarantees and allowed subprocessors per tier; (2) contract term templates and checkbox options for retention windows; (3) a subprocessors disclosure matrix that can be embedded in the contract portal; (4) an SCCs alignment checklist and automated flagging guidance for legal/solutions teams.
acceptance_criteria: Residency catalogue published internally with at least 3 tiers (Global, EU/UK-Only, Customer-VPC) and machine-readable metadata for region and subprocessors
Retention SLA options implemented as contract-level choices (30 days, 90 days, 1 year, custom 30-365) with corresponding pricing delta documented
Subprocessor disclosure matrix populated with current cloud infra and ops subprocessors and a process for 72-hour notification on any change
SCCs alignment doc validated by Legal and Security with a checklist that maps to each residency tier
Pricing experiment framework created: randomized offer exposure for qualifying enterprise signups and metric instrumentation validated
success_metrics: Pilot conversion rate for enterprise trials exposed to residency options >= 18% vs baseline
Average revenue uplift per trial with EU/UK-only option selected >= +12%
Reduction in contract negotiation time for residency-related clauses by 25% (tracked via GTM CRM)
< 3 legal escalations per quarter for subprocessors/retention edge cases during pilot
technical_constraints: Console must display residency tier and retention selection during signup and in the contract builder UI
Billing and rate-limiting must be able to tag customers for residency-tier pricing in backend ledger
Private deployment (VPC) customers require an automated toggle that marks data plane as out-of-band for Hosted metadata
SCCs automation needs extracted artifacts for Legal (data flow diagrams, subprocessors list) from infra inventory (ENG-2847)
legal_notes: Legal prefers discrete contract annexes per residency tier rather than modifying master services agreement text
Retention windows must include clear deletion verification language; avoid 'best efforts' where targeted customers request auditability
SCCs approach: standard EU model clauses + customer appendix for Customer-VPC; Legal requests 2-week review turnaround for first 5 customers
Obtain explicit consent flow for subprocessors where required by local laws (flagged for APAC pilot later)
Escalation path: solution engineers -> legal lead -> security compliance officer (names listed in linked doc)
experiment_design: Between-subjects A/B where enterprise signups are randomly shown either: (A) Basic residency only (control) or (B) tiered residency + priced retention options (treatment)
Stratify by region and ARR band to avoid confounding from large enterprise deals
Primary metric: paid conversion within 30 days. Secondary metrics: time-to-contract, legal escalations, churn at 90 days
Expose pricing delta in checkout and track selection; include optional quote request flow for custom retention beyond 365 days
rollout_plan: Week 1: Publish internal residency catalogue and retention options; enable UI mocks in staging
Week 2: Legal sign-off on templates and SCCs checklist; engineering integration for billing tagging
Week 3: Launch closed pilot (10 customers) via Solutions team; instrument telemetry and contract time tracking
Week 4-6: Monitor metrics; gather qualitative feedback from Solutions/Legal; iterate terms as needed
Post-pilot: Decide rubric to generalize tiers or roll back based on conversion/uplift and legal operational load
